frequency_question: How often does structural friction prevent the execution of announced unilateral executive trade measures within the stated short-term window?
membership_rule: Includes major tariff or quota announcements by U.S. presidents executed via executive authority (e.g., IEEPA, Section 301, Section 232) where implementation was slated within 90 days. Excludes routine statutory adjustments and congressionally passed legislation.

cases.name: Carter Iranian Asset Sanctions / Trade Restrictions (1979)
Trump Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs (2018)

coverage_note: 7 major unilateral executive trade actions identified since 1971; 1 resulted in suspension due to structural/negotiated friction before implementation.
known_gaps: Minor secondary tariff adjustments and threats that did not reach formal presidential proclamation stage are excluded.
skeleton: Executive trade actions with short windows analyzed by historical compliance vs. structural intervention success.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing executive trade authority (like IEEPA and Section 232) remain stable unless major legislative reform occurs.
